chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
Perform salat over whoever dies from among the people of the qiblah, and his reckoning is upon Allah.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقِبْلَةِ: the people of the qiblah; those identified outwardly as Muslims
key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, to Whom ultimate judgment belongs
key_terms.حِسَابُهُ: his reckoning; his final judgment and accountability
key_terms.صَلِّ: perform salat; here, offer the funeral prayer
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; the deceased person in question

ai.seo_question: Should funeral salat be performed for any Muslim from Ahl al-Qiblah?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that funeral salat should be performed for any deceased person who is from Ahl al-Qiblah. It places ultimate judgment of the deceased with Allah, indicating that outward Muslim identity is sufficient for this ruling while final reckoning belongs to Him.
